config.//topics: One ordered topic for every OpenMRS table the cloud server publishes. MirrorMaker
config.//topics2: prefixes it with the alias of the cluster it came from: remote.bahmni-cloud.openmrs.all.
config.//order: One task, one connection and one record per write keep the cloud server's commit order.
config.//restart: THE FIX. Default is false: a connection-level error (e.g. MySQL's 8h
config.//restart2: wait_timeout closing an idle pooled connection overnight) is treated as
config.//restart3: UNRECOVERABLE and kills the task permanently, while the connector still
config.//restart4: reports RUNNING. This direction is the MORE exposed one: users/roles change
config.//restart5: every few days, so its pools idle far longer than the up direction's.
config.//restart6: Safe here because each sink DB is a single instance; the upstream caveat
config.//restart7: about async-replica failover does not apply.
config.//pool: Second layer only -- the primary defence is
config.//pool2: server-side: wait_timeout is 604800 on every node (the stock value is 28800).
config.//pool3: DO NOT set connection.pool.min_size=0: with it, 4 of 13 cloud
config.//pool4: sinks died on boot with 'Unable to determine Dialect without JDBC metadata'.
config.//pool5: Hibernate needs a connection at startup to probe the dialect; an empty pool
config.//pool6: has none. (Until Debezium 3.6 min_size was left at its default of 5; Agroal
config.//pool6b: refuses min > max -- nine sinks FAIL on boot -- so it is 1, stated.)
config.//pool-measured: MEASURED INERT. Two samples 317s apart on both nodes:
config.//pool-measured2: cloud 60 conns aged 512-517s then 829-834s; clinic 35 conns aged 836s.
config.//pool-measured3: Ages tracked wall-clock 1:1 and NOT ONE connection was recycled, so this
config.//pool-measured4: key does not expire idle connections at min_size. Kept for the record, but
config.//pool-measured5: it protects nothing: wait_timeout=604800 is the entire defence. Do not
config.//pool-measured6: count this as a second layer when reasoning about idle connections.
config.//agroal: Survive a MySQL restart and idle-connection closes, on Agroal (Debezium 3.6.2
config.//agroal2: dropped c3p0 for Agroal, DBZ-8899 -- the hibernate.c3p0.* keys below are
config.//agroal3: inert under 3.6.2, same failure shape as connection.pool.timeout was under
config.//agroal4: c3p0: parsed by Hibernate, matched by no active provider, silently dropped.
config.//agroal5: connection.pool.timeout is kept (it is Debezium's own native property, not
config.//agroal6: provider-specific) and set directly; hibernate.agroal.validateOnBorrow is
config.//agroal7: Agroal's checkout-time liveness check, the direct equivalent of c3p0's
config.//agroal9: revalidation interval, the equivalent of c3p0's idle_test_period. Agroal has
config.//agroal10: no configurable test-query hook (no equivalent of preferredTestQuery) --
config.//agroal11: it validates via the JDBC driver's own Connection.isValid(). Same role as
config.//agroal12: the old four keys: survive a MySQL restart, which the server-side
config.//agroal14: kill-45 proof (killed 45 sink connections server-side, next write landed in
config.//agroal15: 5s, every task RUNNING; control sink without these keys FAILED with Broken
config.//agroal16: pipe) was run under c3p0/3.2.4 and has not been independently re-run under
config.//pool-cap: One connection: a single writer keeps the order. Do NOT set min_size=0: the sink dies on boot with 'Unable to determine Dialect'.
config.//table: Each record is written to the table it came from.
config.//keys0: record_key, NOT record_value: delete.enabled REQUIRES record_key, because
config.//keys00: a delete carries after=null and the PK can only come from the key. The up
config.//keys000: direction uses record_value + delete.enabled=false; this direction must
config.//keys0000: propagate deletes, so it uses the key.
config.//keys: record_key carries whatever the source PK was, composite included --
config.//keys3: role_role(parent_role,child_role). No striding is needed in this
config.//keys4: direction: the cloud is the sole writer of these tables.
config.//delete: Deletes MUST propagate. This is how a REVOKED user or role reaches a
config.//delete2: clinic; dropping deletes would leave revoked staff able to log in.
config.//auto: auto.create/auto.evolve are OFF by design here. These tables already exist
config.//auto2: in the clinic's OpenMRS schema; silently creating or altering one would mask
config.//auto3: a genuine schema mismatch instead of surfacing it.
config.//evolution: schema.evolution is the Debezium JDBC sink's own key for the same rule;
config.//evolution2: auto.create/auto.evolve above are another sink's names for it. none = the
config.//evolution3: sink never creates or alters a table, so a column the hub has and this
config.//evolution4: node lacks fails the task loudly instead of changing the clinic's schema
config.//evolution5: outside an upgrade. Stated rather than left to the default.
config.//errors: NOT errors.tolerance=all. 'all' silently DROPS a failing record and
config.//errors2: moves on, so an FK-ordering miss becomes a permanently missing row with only
config.//errors3: a log line. Retry instead, and let a genuine failure be loud.
config.//errors4: include.messages stays FALSE: these payloads are user/provider records.
config.//converters: true on BOTH, matching the source. The JDBC sink needs the schema:
config.//converters2: with schemas.enable=false every task dies on
config.//converters3: 'Configured primary key mode record_key cannot have null schema'.
